summary: mountainash-auth-client follows a clear, consistent structure: auth types live in schemas/, protocol interactions in flows/, connection lifecycle management in mixins/, credential persistence in store/, and callback infrastructure in server/. Each layer follows established naming conventions and re-export patterns, making it straightforward to add new auth types and OAuth providers.
use_cases: Add a new auth type by creating an AuthSpec subclass, registering it in dispatch, and wiring up re-exports
Integrate a new OAuth provider by subclassing a connection mixin with a spec object and provider-specific methods
Write tests following established patterns: FakeSpec/FakeAuth/FakeProfile fixtures, tmp_path for store tests, httpx mocking for token exchanges
Set up a development environment with Hatch, Ruff, and pytest

concepts.name: Module Layout and Conventions
concepts.description: The package is organized into five functional areas: schemas/ for auth type models, flows/ for protocol interactions, mixins/ for connection lifecycle, store/ for persistence, and server/ for callback infrastructure. Auth types use the AuthSpec suffix, flows use the Flow suffix, and mixins use the ConnectionMixin suffix. Public symbols are re-exported through subpackage __init__.py files and the package root __init__.py.

concepts.name: Adding a New Auth Type
concepts.description: Create a new file in schemas/ with an AuthSpec subclass and a unique Literal 'kind' value. Re-export from schemas/__init__.py, then from the package root __init__.py and add to __all__. Optionally register a default mapper in dispatch.py. Add tests in tests/test_schemas.py. All existing auth types follow this same pattern.

concepts.name: Adding a New OAuth Provider
concepts.description: Define a spec object with a .name identifier and a .metadata dictionary containing provider URLs and configuration. Subclass OAuth2ConnectionMixin or OAuth1ConnectionMixin, set the _spec and _base_url class variables, and add any provider-specific methods. The mixin handles token lifecycle automatically.

concepts.name: Test Patterns
concepts.description: Tests use FakeSpec, FakeAuth, and FakeProfile patterns for test isolation. FilesystemStore tests use pytest's tmp_path fixture. Token exchange tests use httpx mocking via unittest.mock.patch. These patterns are consistent across all test files and should be followed for new contributions.

concepts.name: Build and Tooling
concepts.description: The project uses Hatch as its build system (hatchling backend), Ruff for linting (E, F, FA, TCH rules with 120-character line length), pytest for testing with the tests/ directory, and coverage configured for both src/mountainash_auth_client and tests/.
